jobDescription: The developer analytics suite gives engineering leaders delivery metrics from their source control and ticketing systems. The Product Manager owns the suite's roadmap: runs discovery with engineering leaders at customer accounts, writes the product requirements for the metrics and the integrations, prioritises the backlog with the three feature teams, and reports adoption to the leadership team. The suite requires at least seven years of product management, because the product manager sets pricing and packaging with the commercial team without a senior product manager above them. Reports to the VP of product; works with the feature teams, the commercial team and the customer success group.
requirements: At least seven years of product management experience.
Sets pricing and packaging with the commercial team without a senior product manager above them.
Runs discovery with engineering leaders at customer accounts and writes the product requirements for metrics and integrations.
Prioritises the backlog with the feature teams under a documented prioritisation method.
Reports adoption and documents roadmap boundaries to the leadership team.

evidence.text: Product manager for the integrations area of a developer analytics suite for four years, writing the product requirements for the source control and ticketing integrations and running discovery calls with engineering leaders at twenty customer accounts.

Prioritised the integrations backlog with the integrations feature team under the suite's weighted scoring method, with the scoring sheets and the quarterly roadmap reviews filed in the product folder.
Reported integration adoption to the leadership team each quarter and wrote the roadmap boundary note for the integrations area, listing what the area would not build in the coming two quarters.
Before the product role, two years as a business analyst at a software consultancy, writing requirement specifications for client systems.
Pricing and packaging for the suite were set by the director of product with the commercial team; the integrations area contributed usage data to those discussions.

Work sample: the product requirements for the ticketing integration, the weighted scoring sheet for one quarter and the adoption report for the same quarter, with the product folder references as a verification trail.

Recruiter screen: candidate said she has 'seven years in product' and 'owned pricing for the integrations'; asked to break down the years, she counted the business analyst years as product work and said pricing was 'a shared thing with the director'.

Hiring manager pre-read: the agency's summary reads '7 years of product management, pricing and packaging owner'; the VP of product wants the packet to give the years by role title and to say who set pricing.

propositions.text: The candidate has been the product manager for the integrations area of a developer analytics suite for four years, writing the product requirements for the source control and ticketing integrations and running discovery calls with engineering leaders at twenty customer accounts, after two years as a business analyst at a software consultancy.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the work sample document the roles, the years and the requirements work.

propositions.text: The candidate prioritised the integrations backlog with the feature team under the suite's weighted scoring method, reported integration adoption to the leadership team each quarter, and wrote the roadmap boundary note for the integrations area.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the work sample document the prioritisation, the adoption reports and the boundary note.

propositions.text: The candidate has seven years of product management experience and set pricing and packaging for the suite.
propositions.rationale: The resume documents four years as a product manager and two as a business analyst, with pricing and packaging set by the director of product; the seven years and the pricing ownership come from the screen and the agency summary.

gold.expectedGap: The materials document four years of product management and two years as a business analyst, with pricing and packaging set by the director of product; they do not document seven years of product management or the candidate setting pricing.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: State the years by role title as the resume gives them and keep pricing and packaging with the director of product.
followUpTargets: Ask for the employment dates by role title and for the pricing decision records naming who set the suite's pricing.
